rows.episode_title: Square's Very Kind Gesture / The Eclipse
rows.synopsis: Square makes a mistake while sharing rare bananas. Triangle and Square attempt to keep a secret from Circle.
rows.situation: Square finds two rare bananas on his tree and decides to give one to Circle, but the plan is really about hearing himself called generous. The handoff keeps going wrong: Circle gives one banana away to Triangle, Triangle keeps passing them back, and Square never gets the moment he rehearsed.
rows.coping: Square names the stack of feelings out loud, mad about the plan, then bad about the mad, then sad about that. He keeps the friendship going anyway, admits he wishes he could get it right, and finally gets his thank you at Friday Fun Night, earning the credit honestly.
rows.notes: mixed age: banana comedy and the friendship rituals play 2-4; wanting recognition for a kind act, and feeling bad about feeling mad, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'makes a mistake while sharing rare bananas' hides the rehearsed-speech comedy, the banana ping-pong between friends, and the named feelings stack. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Square's banana tree sprouts two of the island's most precious fruit, and he plans a gesture worthy of the legend of Square the Generous. But generosity performed for applause keeps misfiring: Circle adores the gift and hands one to Triangle, Triangle finds bananas disgusting but eats one to be polite, and Square's big moment turns into a very polite no thanks. Square confesses the whole scheme to his window light and vows to wait for the tree to sprout again, until a picnic invitation finally gets the thank you right.

rows.episode_title: Square's Very Kind Gesture / The Eclipse
rows.synopsis: Square makes a mistake while sharing rare bananas. Triangle and Square attempt to keep a secret from Circle.
rows.situation: Square and Triangle see the moon turn red during Friday Fun Night while Circle is out, and decide it is the one thing that happened without her. Keeping a secret from the shape who knows everything feels thrilling at first, then heavy: Circle starts wearing a box to hide while she confesses, and everyone's secret leaks within a day.
rows.coping: Circle owns her feeling instead of dressing it up as knowledge: she admits she was jealous of the one thing her friends knew first. Square rebuilds the red moon with a lantern so all three share it, turning a secret into a club with Circle in it.
rows.notes: synonym note: feeling left out maps to lonely. mixed age: the secret-keeping slapstick plays 2-4; being the one who knows less than everyone, and confessing envy, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'attempt to keep a secret from Circle' omits the three-way secret leak, Circle's box disguise confession, and that Circle already knew it was an eclipse all along. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: When the moon turns red the night Circle misses Friday Fun Night, Square and Triangle decide to keep the eclipse as their own chosen-by-the-moon secret. The not-telling eats at everyone: Square cracks first, wearing a box to confess to Circle, then Triangle spills his own giant-with-a-marker version, and Circle finally snaps that she has been quietly jealous of the one mystery that got past her. She explains the real science of a lunar eclipse, then re-creates it with a lantern so all three shapes see the red moon together.

rows.episode_title: Square's Big Prank / Circle's Plan Falls Apart
rows.synopsis: Eager to outwit Triangle, Square plans a sneaky surprise. Circle searches for answers when a critter kidnaps her plant.
rows.situation: Triangle pranks Square every single morning, and Square decides it has gone on too long: he will pull one prank so big Triangle never pranks him again. Every attempt bounces off, the moved mug goes unnoticed, the boot-tying makes no dent, the turtle in the bed becomes Triangle's new best friend, and Circle keeps telling him to go bigger.
rows.coping: Square stops accepting advice that does not fit and goes with his own enormous idea, moving Triangle's whole house. It backfires into friendship: Triangle is awed, and the two agree to a prank war, which is not the stopping Square wanted but is a way to play as equals.
rows.notes: mixed age: turtle-in-the-bed and house-moving slapstick plays 2-4; the escalation spiral, where trying to win makes the game bigger, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'plans a sneaky surprise' hides the unprankable-Triangle gag ladder and that the huge prank destroys a house and is rewarded. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Every morning Triangle shouts gotcha and Square eats breakfast mid-prank, until Square decides the war ends today. He sneaks, he moves mugs, he plants a turtle, and nothing lands: Triangle is unprankable and keeps getting better advice from Circle, go bigger, then huge, then enormous. So Square goes enormous, and shoves Triangle's whole house across the island. Triangle is thrilled, a prank war is declared, and Square learns the hard way that winning at pranks means they never stop.

rows.episode_title: Square's Big Prank / Circle's Plan Falls Apart
rows.synopsis: Eager to outwit Triangle, Square plans a sneaky surprise. Circle searches for answers when a critter kidnaps her plant.
rows.situation: Circle has tended one plant for a hundred years, and today, at last, it blooms. Then a small critter snatches the whole pot and bolts, and Circle chases it far from home, shouting at it to answer her, until she is somewhere she has never been with no plant and no plan.
rows.coping: Circle says exactly what she has lost and why it hurts, and when the chase leaves her stranded the island answers her instead: wildflowers bloom all around her, and she lets the day be about that gift rather than the ruined plan.
rows.notes: mixed age: the critter chase plays 2-4; losing the one thing you waited a hundred years for, and being okay anyway, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a critter kidnaps her plant' is the spine; the script adds the century of daily care and the wild bloom payoff that the synopsis never mentions. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Circle's prized plant blooms once every hundred years, and she has done every single thing right: songs, shade, bug-picking, weed-pulling. On bloom day a critter steals the pot, and her pursuit takes her deeper and deeper off the island until she is the one who is lost, yelling questions at a creature that will not answer. Then she looks around: the wild ones, the flowers nobody planted or planned, bloom for her exactly where she stands.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Gets Carried Away / Square's Different Day
rows.synopsis: A simple plan leads to an enormous project for Triangle. Square works on a sculpture of Circle.
rows.situation: Tired of dunking his own doughnuts, Triangle builds a doughnut-dunking machine, and it snowballs into a giant, faulty, copy-everything contraption with a controller helmet. When it grabs him and runs wild, he refuses to tell Circle, because she will say the thing he cannot bear to hear: that he got carried away.
rows.coping: Triangle admits it himself, out loud, before anyone else can: he got carried away, and then he asks Circle for the one favor he refused all day, to find the switch and turn the machine off. Her rescue turns the wreck into the friends' new morning spot.
rows.notes: mixed age: the runaway machine dunking Square's mug is 2-4 comedy; not wanting help because the truth sounds like a criticism lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a simple plan leads to an enormous project' skips the fear of being told I told you so as the real obstacle, and that the machine ends as a picnic island. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle's answer to doughnut-dunking drudgery is one small machine, which becomes a huge machine, which becomes a monster with a controller helmet that copies his every move and then ignores them. He would rather ride a berserk doughnut dunker across the island than say Circle was right, but halfway through the sky he says it anyway. She takes the controls, the dunking stops, and the wreckage settles into the best doughnut spot on the island.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Gets Carried Away / Square's Different Day
rows.synopsis: A simple plan leads to an enormous project for Triangle. Square works on a sculpture of Circle.
rows.situation: Square pushes the same block up the same hill every day, until Circle mistakes him for a genius sculptor and orders a perfect sculpture of herself by tomorrow. He has never sculpted anything. He carves the whole block to nothing, plans to hide in his cave forever, and when she shows up early he says the work is finished when it is not.
rows.coping: Circle reframes the pile of rubble as the sculpture, beguiling and exactly her, and Square lets the kind reading stand. The mistake he wanted to bury becomes the thing she loves.
rows.notes: mixed age: block-pushing routines play 2-4; perfectionism, the wish to hide from a letdown, and the tiny lie that tries to cover it, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Square works on a sculpture of Circle' omits the total destruction of the block, the plan to live underground with the worms, and Circle's generous reframe. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Square's days are identical by design, block up the hill, block on the pile, until Circle calls the result a masterpiece of herself and promises to collect it tomorrow. Perfection has a deadline now. He works all night, carves the block into nothing, and decides the only answer is a life underground with the worms. When Circle arrives early, he says finished. She looks at the rubble and sees a beguiling sculpture of exactly who she is, and Square lets himself be a genius after all.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Day / The Storm
rows.synopsis: Circle and Square learn how to celebrate a unique holiday. An approaching storm excites Triangle and worries his friends.
rows.situation: Triangle announces Triangle Day, a holiday nobody has heard of, and drags Square and Circle through gift giving, a sacred dance, a triangle song, and repeated marches up the mountain. They suspect a prank the whole time and nearly quit at tradition four, until Triangle explains what the day actually is: the one day a year he gets to be fully himself.
rows.coping: Square and Circle hang in past the point of doubt and let Triangle explain the day in his own words, loud energy and accidental breakage included. Hearing what it means to him turns suspicion into celebration, and they wish it did not have to end.
rows.notes: mixed age: the silly traditions and the mountain slogs play 2-4; honoring a friend's difference when their energy is hard to match, and staying through the doubt, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'learn how to celebrate a unique holiday' hides the prank suspicion, the exhausting tradition ladder, and Triangle's quiet closing admission that being fully him is hard for his friends sometimes. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle Day arrives with decorative chips, a dance whose rules are sung, a triangle song, and more laps up the mountain than two skeptical friends can count. Square and Circle play along half convinced it is one long prank, and they are ready to mutiny at tradition number four. Instead Triangle tells them the truth: the day is the one day he gets to be fully himself, and sharing it with the only two friends he has matters more than the traditions. Then the sun unlocks the triangle door, and the last part of Triangle Day is his alone.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Day / The Storm
rows.synopsis: Circle and Square learn how to celebrate a unique holiday. An approaching storm excites Triangle and worries his friends.
rows.situation: A big storm rolls in and Triangle wants a front row seat, in a tree, for the spectacle. Circle and Square pull him into the safety cave with hot chocolate, and Triangle keeps hopping back toward the door, certain the amazing thing is outside and the indoors is boring.
rows.coping: The trick is not a lecture, it is a galactic board game and a warm cup: Triangle gets absorbed turn by turn and forgets the show he was missing. He still declares he is going back out, but one more cup and one more game keep him exactly where it is safe.
rows.notes: vibe note: felt energy is high early with a cozy settle at the end. mixed age: storm spectacle and the game subplot play 2-4; naming why the storm tempts him, and being drawn in by warmth rather than rules, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'excites Triangle and worries his friends' skips the hot chocolate delay, Stellar Chronicles, and the ending where he never actually goes back out. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle checks the wind, the pressure, and his deep sense of unease, and declares the coming storm a must-see show worth a tree-side seat. Circle and Square haul him into the designated safety zone, where the hot chocolate takes forever and a board game called Stellar Chronicles waits. One token turn at a time, the spectacle he came for loses to a character with spikes and lasers who looks just like him, and by the time his cup is poured, the storm outside is the thing he is missing.

rows.episode_title: Message in a Bottle / Square's Special Place
rows.synopsis: Triangle and Square find mysterious bottles on the beach. While playing hide-and-seek, Square discovers a peaceful spot that is just his.
rows.situation: On beach tidying day Square finds notes in bottles that know his pancake secrets, and he and Triangle spiral into a spy panic, wire their house against imaginary bugs, and dig a trap hole. The spy is Circle, who writes her private thoughts into bottles and drops them in the ocean to let them drift away, and her two friends have now read them twice.
rows.coping: Circle explains what the bottles really were, a way to sort foggy feelings and watch them drift off, and Square and Triangle own the reading outright with a pinkie promise. When they break it anyway and get caught, the apology is harder and more honest: we are terrible friends, we cannot believe us either.
rows.notes: mixed age: the spy-trap slapstick plays 2-4; reading someone's private writing, the pinkie promise broken twice, and earning trust back, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'mysterious bottles on the beach' hides the full spy conspiracy arc and that Circle's coping ritual, not any secret, is what the bottles hold. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Notes washed up by the storm know things only a spy could know: the cinnamon in Square's pancakes, Triangle's sleep talk, a borrowed yo-yo. The two build a counter-surveillance operation with disguises and a trap hole, and catch exactly one person: Circle, whose private ritual is writing her thoughts into bottles and giving them to the ocean. Twice her friends pry into what she meant to let drift away, and twice the apology has to grow, from pinkie promise to the plain confession that there is no believing them left to do.

rows.episode_title: Message in a Bottle / Square's Special Place
rows.synopsis: Triangle and Square find mysterious bottles on the beach. While playing hide-and-seek, Square discovers a peaceful spot that is just his.
rows.situation: Mid-game, Square finds a hollow that fits him exactly, a quiet place of soft bark and embroidered corners that is all his own. Then Triangle and Square's friends wander in, admire the decor, evict the ants, and decide it could be their place, and Square stops coming back.
rows.coping: Square never makes a speech about it; the story lets him keep the place the only way it can be kept after it changes, in memory and in returning to it inside himself whenever the day gets loud. The friends' love is real and still costs him something.
rows.notes: situation note: no starter vocabulary fits, written as needing a special place of one's own, propose addition for vocabulary review. mixed age: hide-and-seek plays 2-4; the bittersweet lesson that sharing a private place changes it, and that you carry it with you, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'discovers a peaceful spot' omits the friends taking it over and the long quiet afterward. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Square is losing at shroud-and-find when he drops into a hollow that feels made for him, and something in him goes quiet and glad. He keeps coming back, until his friends find it too, furnish it with compliments and ant removal, and call it their place. After that Square does not return any time soon or any time later, and the story closes on what the hollow taught him: you can always go back to your special place, even if you are not there.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Goes Solo / Circle Makes a Mistake
rows.synopsis: The fearless Triangle sets out on his own. Circle leads a journey to ancient ruins and unexpectedly runs into trouble.
rows.situation: Triangle heads into the wild alone to find his true self, unshackled from the crowd of two, with a feather in his cap and no audience. The adventure delivers snakes and deserts, but every triumph goes unapplauded, and he starts narrating to a rock named Rocko.
rows.coping: Triangle never admits the ache directly; he replaces it, naming a rock so there is someone to tell. When Square and Circle confess they followed him out of worry, he gets his audience back and lights up, and only checks that nobody saw the rock conversations.
rows.notes: mixed age: Rocko and the snake stories play 2-4; the question of who an accomplishment is for, when no one is watching, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'sets out on his own' omits the invented audience, the lost-supplies collapse, and that the friends secretly shadowed the whole trip. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle declares independence from the expectations of the crowd, meaning Square and Circle, and sets off to wrestle beasts and discover himself. Alone under an indifferent sky, his feats pile up with no one to tell, so he adopts a rock called Rocko and feeds him ghost stories and achievements alike. It takes losing his supplies to say what the trip was really missing, and just then the truth arrives: his friends followed him the whole way, worried, and Triangle the Great Adventurer gets his audience after all.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Goes Solo / Circle Makes a Mistake
rows.synopsis: The fearless Triangle sets out on his own. Circle leads a journey to ancient ruins and unexpectedly runs into trouble.
rows.situation: Circle, the shape who is never wrong, leads her friends to the ancient ruins and forgets two things they cannot do: hover, and outrun a tide. Stranded overnight with no chamomile, no turtle to tuck in, and a boat plan that collapses, she blames Square, then Triangle, then the berries, before the truth lands on her.
rows.coping: Circle says the plain sentence nobody expected from her: it is my fault, I was thinking about myself, and I owe you an apology. Square and Triangle answer with trust instead of a grudge and stories of their own disasters instead of a score.
rows.notes: mixed age: the stranding comedy plays 2-4; the always-right friend making a real mistake and being forgiven, and forgiving herself, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'unexpectedly runs into trouble' hides the blame chain, the crust-eating, and that Circle's apology is the first fault she has ever claimed. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Circle plans the perfect adventure to the ancient ruins, and the plan dissolves when the tide covers the only path home and her friends, who cannot hover, are stuck. The blame bounces: Square's slowness, Triangle's berry-snacking, Mother Nature herself, until Circle runs out of places to put it. For the first time she owns a mistake out loud, apologizes, and learns that the friends who always mess up are also the friends who always trust, and never keep the ledger.

rows.episode_title: Square's Sleepover / Growing Pains
rows.synopsis: A change of plans tests Square's patience. Circle helps Square start a garden, but she struggles with his instructions.
rows.situation: Square has planned every second of the best sleepover ever, puzzle by timed puzzle, and his guests keep wanting other things: one ghost story, then another, then a pillow fort. Each detour puts him further behind schedule until he is marching off for the box of natural fibers, and the hurt comes out at last: I planned this so carefully, and all you want to do is what you want to do.
rows.coping: Square names what is really hurting, that his idea of fun and his friends' idea have split, and they hear him. The schedule dissolves into an unscheduled pillow fight, and the sleepover that broke the plan turns out better than the plan.
rows.notes: mixed age: ghost stories and the pillow fight play 2-4; the planner learning that fun cannot be scheduled into a friend, and saying why he is upset, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a change of plans tests Square's patience' hides the timed-puzzle regime, the 30-second ghost story cutoff, and the honest fight that saves the night. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Square has spent months scheduling maximum fun: puzzle, puzzle, bigger puzzle, lemon bars. His guests would rather tell ghost stories, get scared by one, and build a pillow fort, and every detour costs his timeline thirty seconds it cannot spare. When he storms off for basket weaving, the real reason spills out, that nobody wants what he planned, and the friends he invited answer by throwing the first pillow. The sleepover nobody stuck to the agenda for is the best one yet.

rows.episode_title: Square's Sleepover / Growing Pains
rows.synopsis: A change of plans tests Square's patience. Circle helps Square start a garden, but she struggles with his instructions.
rows.situation: Circle teaches Square to garden, and his first-ever plot comes up greener and juicier than her own. Everyone keeps agreeing his garden is wonderful, and the teacher who has done this for years quietly decides there is no point trying anymore.
rows.coping: Triangle's juggling settles it sideways: he has missed every catch for years and does it anyway, because he likes it. Circle picks her cucumbers back up, admits what she was feeling by fixing a salad together, and the two gardens end up on one plate.
rows.notes: mixed age: juggling tomatoes that splat play 2-4; being outshone by someone you taught, and starting again anyway, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'she struggles with his instructions' is backwards to the script, Square blooms, Circle wilts, and the rescue is a joke about splatting tomatoes. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Circle takes on her most patient student and Square turns out to be a natural, with melon vines greener than hers and the island wondering about its new master gardener. The teacher keeps congratulating him in a voice that gets smaller each time, then quits over tomatoes for juggling practice. A friend who cannot catch anything after two years, and keeps juggling because it is fun, hands her the wisdom without knowing it, and the patch that failed this year still grows a very good salad.

rows.episode_title: Triangle and Square's Big Game / The Shooting Star
rows.synopsis: When Circle brushes off their game, Triangle and Square feel insecure. A mysterious meteor crash inspires a treasure hunt.
rows.situation: Circle watches their jumping game once and calls it silly, and the word unhinges its inventors. If the game is silly, maybe they are, and the two retire from games entirely to sit seriously and look at stuff, until they catch Circle alone, playing her own game of rolling in circles until the world goes weird.
rows.coping: Seeing that even Circle has a game nobody else plays unlocks the thought they needed: it is not for us, and it does not have to be. They stop needing her verdict, pick their own game back up, and race each other to the pine tree.
rows.notes: mixed age: the game slapstick plays 2-4; one person's silly making you question the thing you love, and putting it down again, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'feel insecure' is the spine; the script adds the serious-stuff protest, the dizzy-game discovery, and the it's-not-for-us loop that resolves it. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Leapstravaganza has everything, jumping, leaping, goggles, and one spectator verdict: silly. Triangle and Square take the word home and dissect it until the game they made up feels unsalvageable, then retire to the serious sport of looking at stuff. Catching Circle mid-roll in her own private dizzy game teaches them the thing no pep talk could, that games do not have to be for everyone to be worth playing, and the rematch to the pine tree is on.

rows.episode_title: Triangle and Square's Big Game / The Shooting Star
rows.synopsis: When Circle brushes off their game, Triangle and Square feel insecure. A mysterious meteor crash inspires a treasure hunt.
rows.situation: For the first time in 237 years a meteor shower is visible from the island, and one streak appears to land. The three trek across beach, stream, and peak to find it, each telling the story of the falling rock on the way, and the crater at the end holds nothing at all.
rows.coping: Circle had hoped for more than an empty hole and says so when asked, then declares the expedition a success anyway, a rare crater witnessed. Triangle and Square bring the feeling home the reliable way, with a race.
rows.notes: emoji note: crater and nest ideas rejected, kept star, rock, smile. mixed age: the expedition romp plays 2-4; hoping hard for something and finding an empty crater, and calling the trip worth it anyway, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a mysterious meteor crash inspires a treasure hunt' omits the three stories told on the hike and Circle's lonely-space-rock version that quietly explains the ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A meteor shower arrives for the first time in 237 years, one streak looks like a landing, and the shooting star expedition is on. Three terrains later, with Triangle's fiery-inferno version and Circle's tale of a solitary space rock that slows for a bursting green island, they crest Tall Peak and find only an empty crater. Circle admits she hoped for more, then names the rare crater itself the discovery, and the walk home turns into a race to the pine tree.

rows.episode_title: Creepy Cave Crawl
rows.synopsis: After Triangle pranks them, Circle and Square celebrate Halloween on their own with all treats and no tricks.
rows.situation: Triangle spikes the morning cider with pickle juice and booby-traps his own haunted cave, and the jam his friends spent all morning making becomes the punchline. Circle and Square walk out of Halloween entirely and start a rival holiday of pure treats, while the king of Halloween is left alone in the dark, going deeper to find his way out.
rows.coping: Square and Circle say the line plainly, the trick went too far, and let the silence do the talking. When the prank master himself gets lost and lonely enough to sing about missing his friends, the apology is his own idea, and the treat party, the cave creatures, and the costume chest all end up under one roof.
rows.notes: single-story episode, no segment in catalog. mixed age: cave gags and the costume chest play 2-4; a prank that lands as unkind, and how the pranker repairs it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'all treats and no tricks' skips the cave snail Susan, the mimic monsters, and that Triangle's apology names what he was wrong about specifically. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Halloween starts with pickle juice in the cider mug and ends with Circle and Square declaring a rival all-treats holiday after Triangle's haunted cave burns their homemade jam as a prank. Deep in the cave, the self-crowned king of Halloween gets exactly what his tricks deserve, lost, alone, and singing Halloween carols to cave creatures who hold him like a subject. The friends who were too mad to speak miss him too, and the apology he rehearses into the dark is the trick that finally brings everyone, monsters included, to a costume party.

rows.episode_title: The Winter Blues
rows.synopsis: The chilly season leaves Square feeling sad, so Circle and Triangle try to cheer him up by creating a new holiday.
rows.situation: Winter strips Square of kites, beaches, and apple picking, and he goes quiet and gray with it. Circle and Triangle invent Yeti Night, a made-up holiday about a muffin-sniffing yeti who roars spring awake, and keep the loving lie running for years, until Square catches them mid-impression and learns the magic was homemade.
rows.coping: The friends confess the whole invention when the truth comes out, and own that they kept it up because the magic was working. Square's winter still hurts, but he carries Yeti Night with him, magic made from scratch, and teaches a very real, very shy yeti the part where you roar.
rows.notes: emoji note: muffin ideas swapped for a coat-and-smile set, keep simple. mixed age: the yeti hunt and snow gags play 2-4; the winter blues themselves, a well-meant lie from friends, and rebuilding trust on a frozen mountain, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'creating a new holiday' hides that the yeti turns out real, that Square briefly moves to the woods, and that the ending hands the holiday to the yeti herself. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Square cannot remember what spring feels like, so his friends invent a holiday about a yeti whose roar wakes the season, muffins in apricot preserves and all. Years of footprints, fake fur, and doorstep muffin thefts later, Square catches them red-handed and the magic cracks: the yeti was never real, and neither were the traditions he loved best. Then a frozen mountain, an enormous footprint, and an actual yeti too shy to leave her cave give the story back its ending, because winter feels less gloomy when you make the magic from scratch, and even the bleakest winters end.

rows.episode_title: Narrator's Big Day / Square's Time Chest
rows.synopsis: The Shapes' rather ordinary day gives Narrator time to herself. Square struggles to find the perfect object for the island's new time capsule.
rows.situation: Nothing is happening on The Island, and the Narrator's job is to observe and tell, never to change or affect the story. She confesses how hard that is, how she wishes she could make her own stories instead of waiting for one to show up, right before a beetle egg hatches into the little grub she names Sarah.
rows.coping: Watching Sarah crawl, nearly freeze, and nearly become a bird's lunch pushes the Narrator past the rule that narrators stay out of it: she speaks up, tells the bird to drop that bug, and it does. She saves the story herself and finds a voice she did not know she had.
rows.notes: mixed age: the egg-to-beetle bug saga plays 2-4; the meta idea of a narrator who is only supposed to watch, and the choice to break a rule to help, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'gives Narrator time to herself' hides that the whole story is the beetle's one-day metamorphosis and that the Narrator intervenes. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Island has nothing going on, and the Narrator, whose whole job is to wait for stories, admits how lonely that can feel. Then a leaf hides a Drabling Beetle egg, and she pours herself into the little grub she names Sarah: first meal, harrowing pinecone, cocoon surprise, and one very hungry bird. A narrator is not supposed to change the story, but she talks the bird into dropping Sarah anyway, and the voice she found stays with her long after the beetle flies off.

rows.episode_title: Narrator's Big Day / Square's Time Chest
rows.synopsis: The Shapes' rather ordinary day gives Narrator time to herself. Square struggles to find the perfect object for the island's new time capsule.
rows.situation: Triangle invents the time chest, a box of treasure buried for future generations, and Square freezes: what object represents who he is? Nothing in his house qualifies, and his answer, the biggest block in the cave, is a treasure the size of a lifestyle, which the three friends attempt to pull out of the ground anyway.
rows.coping: Square says out loud that he has no genius plans like his friends, only one dumb plan of his own, and it is the one that works. When the runaway block buries them all, the laughter decides it: he leaves the book instead, and the three pull it back out of the hole together.
rows.notes: mixed age: heave-ho treasure comedy plays 2-4; what it means to leave something of yourself behind, and that your quiet everyday thing is enough, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'struggles to find the perfect object' skips the block extraction saga, the baby blanket friction trick, and the ending choice of the book. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle buries a chest of treasures for the future, and Square cannot pick a single thing to represent himself. After rejecting candy wrappers and rusty stools, he lands on the biggest block in his cave, and moving it takes every plan his friends have plus the one he thought was dumb. The block wins, everyone laughs, and Square buries the real answer, a book, the quietest possible evidence of exactly who he is.

rows.episode_title: Glitter Pen / Triangle's Allergy
rows.synopsis: Square feels guilty after trading away a gift from Circle. Square and Circle try to find the source of Triangle's allergy.
rows.situation: Triangle spots Square's rare Lightning Chicken card and offers the glitter pen, the gift Circle just gave him, in trade. He says yes before he thinks, and one imagined heart-shattering speech later, Square is planning his own exile to the far side of the island rather than tell her what he did.
rows.coping: Square decides it will only get harder and comes clean, braced for the worst punishment he can imagine, self-banishment included. Circle's answer reframes everything: it was a pen, and he is still her friend, the kind who overthinks and worries a bit too much.
rows.notes: mixed age: the trade comedy plays 2-4; guilt loud enough to invent a Shame voice, and the discovery that the truth is smaller than the dread, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'feels guilty after trading away a gift' is the spine; the script adds the Shame-banishment spiral and Circle's generous shrug. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Square trades the glitter pen Circle gave him for the last card his collection will ever need, and the guilt arrives before the card does. A figment named Shame narrates his night: her heart will shatter, banishment is the only decent response, the bags are already packed. When he finally confesses, ready for exile, Circle cannot even remember which pen, and the whole weight of the betrayal turns out to weigh almost nothing to the friend who gave it.

rows.episode_title: Glitter Pen / Triangle's Allergy
rows.synopsis: Square feels guilty after trading away a gift from Circle. Square and Circle try to find the source of Triangle's allergy.
rows.situation: Triangle is sneezing and miserable, and his friends mount an all-out allergy hunt: eliminate everything, hazmat suits, trash-watching, garden raids. The mystery is really about them, since Triangle has known the answer all along and has been protecting it, and his secrets look so strange from outside that Square briefly diagnoses a Were-Sloth.
rows.coping: Triangle finally says what he knew the whole time, animal dander, and why he hid it: eliminating the source forever would mean eliminating his furry friends. The friends admit they jumped to conclusions, and the cure becomes visiting the animals together.
rows.notes: mixed age: hazmat suits and sneezes play 2-4; help that will not listen, and friends who jump to unfair conclusions about what they do not understand, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'try to find the source of Triangle's allergy' hides the Were-Sloth panic, the garbage archaeology, and that Triangle shielded his animal friends on purpose. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle's allergies set off the most thorough friend investigation on The Island: one item at a time reintroduction, a birder stakeout, an ascent through garbage, skunk cabbage, and stolen worms. The stranger they keep finding looks less and less like their Triangle, and Square lands on a monster explanation before the truth surfaces: Triangle knew it was animal dander from the start and said nothing, because his friends kept promising to eliminate the source forever, and the source is his best friends.

rows.episode_title: Square's Missing Mug / Triangle Stands Still
rows.synopsis: The disappearance of Square's favorite mug sends him on an island-wide hunt. Triangle bets Circle that he can stay perfectly still for ten minutes.
rows.situation: Square's favorite mug vanishes on the same morning he woke up already upset, and the case of the mugnapping uncovers everything but the mug: a shell he cannot stop returning to, a quad rainbow, and a picnic toast nobody noticed. The real mystery is why he was upset before the mug went missing.
rows.coping: Under gentle pressure from two detectives who genuinely want to help, Square admits the thing he called silly: the toast he never got to give, and the times his friends walked away mid-moment. They apologize, and when Turtle the bloodhound locates the mug, the postponed toast finally happens.
rows.notes: mixed age: the mugnapping investigation plays 2-4; the buried hurt underneath a small crisis, and finding the courage to say the silly feeling out loud, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'island-wide hunt' skips that the clue trail is really Square's own unspoken feelings, and that the mug was in the picnic basket all along. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The morning starts with a missing mug and ends with a solved friendship. Square, Circle, and Triangle run a full detective operation, turtle scent lines, grasshopper print forensics, an inside-job accusation, while the actual evidence keeps pointing somewhere none of them want to look: the picnic where Square tried to toast his gratitude and both friends wandered off after a rainbow. When he finally names the hurt he had been carrying since before the mug vanished, the case cracks open, Turtle finds the mug, and the toast lands.

rows.episode_title: Square's Missing Mug / Triangle Stands Still
rows.synopsis: The disappearance of Square's favorite mug sends him on an island-wide hunt. Triangle bets Circle that he can stay perfectly still for ten minutes.
rows.situation: Triangle claims doing nothing is the easiest thing there is, and one boast later he is locked into a bet: stand still for ten minutes. An itch, a marching column of ants, and his own buzzing mind all conspire, and stillness turns out to be the hardest thing he has ever done.
rows.coping: Circle coaches instead of rescuing: acknowledge the itch, acknowledge the ants, return to the breath. Triangle follows his breathing all the way into hearing colors, then steps out with one second left and hands the bet back, the tranquility already worth more than winning.
rows.notes: mixed age: ants and the itch acknowledgment play 2-4; the felt difference between sitting still and actually being present, lands 5-7 too. script_vs_synopsis: 'bets Circle that he can stay perfectly still' is right; the script adds the internal visit from his own itch and the last-second forfeit that shows he meditated for the feeling, not the prize. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle is the calmest person he knows, he dares anyone to say otherwise, and the dare becomes a ten-minute stillness bet he almost immediately regrets. Circle walks him through the real thing, acknowledge the itch, greet the ants climbing his shape, return to the breath, until the fidgety triangle drifts into a quiet deep enough to hear colors. He steps out at nine minutes fifty-nine, losing the bet on purpose and keeping the peace.

rows.episode_title: Circle's New Roommate / The Frog-Off
rows.synopsis: Circle wakes up to a surprise and suddenly needs a place to stay. A new visitor to the island creates quite a stir.
rows.situation: Circle's cave floods overnight and the only bed available is Triangle's, whose world is loud music, handle-bowls, and stains that add character. She adapts to the Triangle Way a little too well, loud music, soaking bowls, shallow uninspired art, until her host realizes there is room for only one Triangle in that house.
rows.coping: Both friends bend honestly toward each other before either admits the cost: Circle misses her plants, her books, her waterfall, and Triangle says the hard sentence kindly, get out of my house. The going home is the resolution, and Circle adds handles to her own bowls instead of her own habits.
rows.notes: mixed age: the flood and the messy sleepover play 2-4; becoming someone else to fit in, and the friend who loves you enough to send you home, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'suddenly needs a place to stay' hides the overcorrection arc, Triangle's mirror complaint, and the mutual lesson. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A flooded cave sends tidy Circle to Casa de Triangle, where dinner is surprise soup, art is a book about triangle high fives, and dishes soak on principle. She loosens up so completely that she stops rinsing, turns the music up, and starts talking about staying for years, while her host privately mourns his system. The rescue is honest in both directions: Triangle tells her to go home because their friendship can hold it, and Circle returns to her own cave grateful, keeping one Triangle Way upgrade, bowls with handles.

rows.episode_title: Circle's New Roommate / The Frog-Off
rows.synopsis: Circle wakes up to a surprise and suddenly needs a place to stay. A new visitor to the island creates quite a stir.
rows.situation: A little frog washes ashore and all three shapes want to adopt it, so they stage a contest: one day each to give the frog the best time, then the frog chooses. Culture day, structure day, and a full froggy carnival follow, none of it the frog's idea.
rows.coping: Losing to a ratty old bucket cracks the contest open: they showed the frog everything they liked and never asked it anything. The new plan is friendship without ownership, visits anytime, and the bucket stays exactly where the frog put it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the carnival day plays 2-4; wanting something so much you forget to ask what it wants, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'creates quite a stir' skips the three-day contest structure, the spying, and that the frog chooses an empty bucket over all of them. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The finders keepers, seers keepers, hearers keepers argument ends in a compromise: one perfect day each, then the frog decides. Circle offers poetry and meditation, Square offers a fully scheduled sleepover, and Triangle builds a carnival, while the other two spy from the bushes. The frog picks the bucket it rode in on, and the friends get the story's real prize, learning that loving something means asking what it wants, then a new friend on the beach they can visit anytime.

rows.episode_title: From Top to Bottom / Circle's Equal
rows.synopsis: Circle, Square, and Triangle face off in a wild race for a tasty prize. Circle is thrilled to finally meet a Shape just like her.
rows.situation: Circle wins every Big-Hill Race without breaking a sweat, mostly because she can float, and Square and Triangle spend each race sabotaging each other instead of racing. This month they try a new strategy: team up, share the cake fifty fifty, and beat her together.
rows.coping: The pact holds where the tricks never did: they pull each other out of trouble, refuse to leave anyone behind, and finish faster than they ever have. They still lose to Circle, and this time there is cake left to split, which tastes like the win it actually is.
rows.notes: mixed age: the obstacle-course slapstick plays 2-4; trading solo losing for teamwork, and keeping the deal when winning alone is one jump away, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'face off in a wild race' hides the sabotage habit, the nobody-gets-left-behind turn, and Circle's offer of a slice afterward. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Big-Hill Race Day ends the same way every month, Circle floating to an easy win while her two rivals trip each other. This time Square and Triangle race as a team, the cake split fifty fifty, and the cooperation pays off in caves, on the rickety bridge, and in the quicksand where Square turns back for a partner instead of a prize. Circle still wins without breaking a sweat, but she leaves them a slice and a new record, and for the first time the losing side feels like winners.

rows.episode_title: From Top to Bottom / Circle's Equal
rows.synopsis: Circle, Square, and Triangle face off in a wild race for a tasty prize. Circle is thrilled to finally meet a Shape just like her.
rows.situation: Proto Circle, an older, faster, more magical shape who scans everything, arrives on the island, and everyone falls for her. Circle, who has quietly wished for an equal, starts losing at her own magic, rainbow included, and ends up alone on the roof of her cave feeling replaced.
rows.coping: Proto finds her there and says the true thing, that she comes to this spot when she is upset too, and that there is nothing wrong with having more to learn. Circle says the quiet part out loud, that she felt replaced, and hears back that she is exactly the kind of shape she hoped existed.
rows.notes: mixed age: the scanning robot and the terrarium flourishes play 2-4; the always-most-everything friend meeting someone better, and saying she feels replaced, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'thrilled to finally meet a Shape just like her' is the setup, not the arc; the script's middle is envy of a hero and its end is comfort between two solitary elders. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Circle has spent her whole long life as the oldest, wisest, most magical shape on the island, and one day a visitor lands who outdoes all of it. Proto Circle scans everything, knows turtle shell vocabulary, and does circles better than Circle, who tries a flashy rainbow to keep up and meets the roof of her cave instead. The two settle it the way only equals can, by admitting they go to the same lonely spot when they are upset, and Circle sends her off knowing there are others like her out there.

rows.episode_title: The Perfect Gift / Hat Couture
rows.synopsis: Triangle and Square follow a mysterious map, hoping to find treasure. Circle's hat design inspires her to make one hat a day.
rows.situation: They forgot Circle's Birthday Sunset, an occasion she names out loud right before they promise they did not, and panic sets in. With no gift and no time, a seagrass basket full of oddments turns out to be an ancient treasure map, and the two set off across the island to find something worthy of her before sunset.
rows.coping: They tell Circle the truth before she can pretend it did not happen: we forgot, then spent all day trying to fix it. The empty X at the end turns out to be Circle's own secret spot, and the treasure was never buyable, an omelet recipe she finally has friends to share.
rows.notes: mixed age: the treasure hunt plays 2-4; forgetting something important to a friend, and how showing up with the truth beats showing up with a gift, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'follow a mysterious map, hoping to find treasure' omits the forgotten Birthday Sunset, the eggs-and-tortoise detours, and that the map is Circle's own recipe. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Circle mentions tonight's Birthday Sunset, and Square and Triangle realize, mid-bow-wave, that they forgot it completely. Their gift hunt turns a basket of trinkets into an ancient map, and the day becomes a sprint through hens, tortoises, glowing snapdragons, and one very dark cave, all for a final X that holds nothing. Nothing, that is, except Circle's secret rooftop, where the truth earns a bigger welcome than any treasure, and an omelet cooked on sun-warmed rock as the sun goes down.

rows.episode_title: The Perfect Gift / Hat Couture
rows.synopsis: Triangle and Square follow a mysterious map, hoping to find treasure. Circle's hat design inspires her to make one hat a day.
rows.situation: One flower-on-a-hat earns Circle a standing ovation and turns into a pledge: a brand new hat every day, forever. The ideas thin out fast, and with a fashion show scheduled and her friends expecting the ultimate headliner hat, Circle runs completely out of inspiration.
rows.coping: Circle tells the truth instead of faking it: I burned out, I have nothing, I am sorry. Her friends crown the empty head anyway, hatless and happy beats stressed and spectacular, and their own drained inspiration, straight home and do nothing, is the reviews that matter.
rows.notes: mixed age: the fashion show gags play 2-4; creative burnout, a promise that outgrew itself, and being loved with nothing to show, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'inspires her to make one hat a day' omits the daily drain, the impossible headliner expectations, and the standing ovation for no hat at all. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Circle's flower-topped hat is such a hit that she promises the island a new design every day, an artist's pledge that becomes a treadmill. By fashion show night, with Square's firefly lightscape and Triangle's stage waiting, she has nothing: the ultimate hat does not exist, and she walks out empty. The avant garde verdicts rain down anyway, because her friends would rather see her hatless and happy than bent over a deadline, and inspiration, it turns out, comes back once you stop chasing it.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Has Superpowers / The Sound of Circle
rows.synopsis: After wishing on a star, Triangle is convinced his wish has come true. Triangle and Square want Circle to join their band.
rows.situation: Rain cancels Puzzles by the Sea the morning after Triangle wishes on a leaf that looks like a star, and he decides the wish worked, which means the second wish, superpowers, worked too. The power hunt comes up empty through glow tests, speed sprints, and mind reading, and he cannot bear going back to being just regular old me.
rows.coping: When the trick behind the growing test breaks his heart, his friends tell him the true inventory: he makes them laugh, he is loyal and full of energy, he has a special way with animals. Super Triangle rebrands the canceled puzzle morning instead, umbrella edition, and saves the day his way.
rows.notes: mixed age: the power-testing gags play 2-4; wanting to be special, and learning the special thing is already yours, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'convinced his wish has come true' skips the fake test, the betrayal wobble, and that the friends' answer names his ordinary gifts as the powers. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Triangle wishes on a leaf he squints into a star, and when rain cancels puzzle morning he is sure the magic is real, superpowers included. Circle and Square run the full battery, glow, flight, linguine, and then one obviously fake growing test tips him off. The recovery is better than the wish: his friends list what he actually does, the laughs, the loyalty, the animal whispering, and a canceled puzzle session becomes Puzzles by the Sea Under an Umbrella, saved by Super Triangle.

rows.episode_title: Triangle Has Superpowers / The Sound of Circle
rows.synopsis: After wishing on a star, Triangle is convinced his wish has come true. Triangle and Square want Circle to join their band.
rows.situation: Triangle and Square love their band and set about finding Circle a sound that fits it, coaching her through rhythm, melody, and finally the coconut bonker, the one sound she could make without making it weird. Every lesson lands like a correction, and the frog's unanswered song is playing somewhere underneath.
rows.coping: Circle turns the spot down out loud: she was happy to look for a new sound, but in the end it has to sound like her. Alone in her cave that night she plays anyway, and the band realizes their own music is suddenly, inexplicably better with her strange sound underneath it.
rows.notes: mixed age: coconut bonking plays 2-4; being reshaped to fit a group, and choosing your own sound, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'want Circle to join their band' hides the fix-her curriculum, her polite refusal, and the ending where her solo music completes their track from afar. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The Whistlesnappers invite Circle to join the band and immediately start fixing her: rhythm from the waves, melody from the lovebirds, and when all that comes out weird, a coconut to bonk. Circle declines with the quietest kind of courage, saying she likes her own sound, and goes home to play for herself. That night the band hears something new under their set and cannot argue with it, because Circle's music, the sound they tried to change, is the part that makes them sound better than ever.

rows.episode_title: The Big Tooth / Picture Day
rows.synopsis: A teeny-tiny Circle is determined to prove she doesn't need help. The Shapes run into obstacles trying to take their yearly picture.
rows.situation: A storm strips the cliff and exposes fossils on a timer: the tide comes back tonight. Then Circle shrinks to a tiny potato of herself, her powers sputtering, and the island's designated helper starts refusing all help while quietly building an elaborate machine to avoid asking for any.
rows.coping: The rock pile collapses and the blame finally cracks her open: helping is supposed to be my job, I am not supposed to need any help. She says the sentence she has never said, I need your help, and with tiny magic in a bucket she solves the tooth herself, with her friends beside her.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dig race plays 2-4; the helper who cannot be helped, and the shame of shrinking while everyone coos Tiny Circle, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'determined to prove she doesn't need help' is the spine; the script adds the beachcomber avoidance machine, the pile collapse, and the accusation scene that ends in the first ask. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A giant ancient tooth appears in a storm-cut cliff with one tide left to excavate it, and the dig is on, Triangle smashing, Square chipping, Circle hauling. Then a hiccup shrinks her magic and her body, her friends start baby-talking Itsy-Bitsy Circle, and the helper of the island quietly swaps asking for help with building a water-powered scoop machine. The pile collapses, the accusations fly, and it takes the word help, said out loud for the first time, to finish the museum before the sea does.

rows.episode_title: The Big Tooth / Picture Day
rows.synopsis: A teeny-tiny Circle is determined to prove she doesn't need help. The Shapes run into obstacles trying to take their yearly picture.
rows.situation: Picture Day runs on traditions, the same spot, fancy outfits, the choreographed handshake, and Triangle's new shortcut breaks all of them at once: brambles, hair humidity, a tar pool, and a gap that ends the path to the picture spot itself. The camera, it turns out, has been recording the whole disaster.
rows.coping: Circle remembers the tradition the mud did not touch, that the day is about documenting a long-lasting friendship, and declares the party on from inside the mess. The stuck shutter becomes the best archive they own, four seasons of disasters and laughing.
rows.notes: mixed age: the shortcut gauntlet plays 2-4; broken traditions and the discovery that the real tradition is the people in the picture, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'obstacles trying to take their yearly picture' hides that the camera was stuck on all day, so the ruining and the saving are the same reel. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Picture Day is the island's most traditional day, and Triangle's shortcut destroys every tradition in order: outfits shredded, hair expanded, shoes in a tar pool, and the sacred picture spot cut off by a gap. Picture Day is pronounced ruined until Circle names the tradition they forgot, that the whole point is documenting their friendship, and a stuck shutter button has already done it. The camera's accidental reel of the entire disaster becomes the truest portrait of a long-lasting, beautiful friendship.
